component.name: OpenXplorer Native Preview
component.summary: Preview of the native OpenXplorer file manager

description.p: A preview of the next OpenXplorer, drawn with native GTK 4 widgets instead of a web page. It browses local folders, SMB shares and connected phones in the familiar tabbed window styled after Windows 11 File Explorer.
The preview is incomplete and runs beside the current OpenXplorer without replacing it. It never changes file associations, browser preferences or network mounts.

A name being renamed in place no longer closes when you use its own right-click menu, such as Paste or Select All, or switch to another window. Item check boxes are off by default, so a selected item is only highlighted, as in Windows; View > Item check boxes turns them back on.

Folder Options replaces Adjust view display style, with Windows' General and View tabs, and Windows Explorer's Ctrl+E, Ctrl+D, F11 and Alt+P work. The Share button emails the selected files through the desktop's email app. Delete moves items to the Recycle Bin wherever it works and asks only about items that cannot go there. As in Windows Explorer, a file operation that succeeds or is cancelled says nothing and sends no desktop notification, while failures, and failures not yet shown when you cancel, are still reported; read-only drives are not singled out, and New and Paste stay on in folders you cannot write to; Undo stays on Ctrl+Z and the folder menu. Keys meant for an open dialog no longer reach the files behind it, menus show in full when they fit on the monitor, submenus open in the same popup, a cut item pasted into its own folder stays put, and a failed copy names the real file.

Make OpenXplorer default also sends other apps' Open and Save dialogs to OpenXplorer, and GTK 3 apps use them too after the next login. Format on a removable drive opens OpenXplorer's own Format dialog instead of GNOME Disks, and Enter in Extract all extracts. Deleting many files on a share asks the server about each file once instead of three times. A move between drives keeps the source files of a folder it skipped partway, Undo asks first when it cannot check a whole copy, signing out of a server forgets its passwords on every port, and the Recycle Bin and search results no longer show stale items.

Brave's downloads, its Save page as and Save as PDF, and its upload dialogs can open OpenXplorer's own Open and Save dialogs, also when the desktop portal reads its settings from a different folder, and the Brave sync can make Brave ask where to save each download. A Save dialog names the file for the type chosen in it. By default, an unselected item's check box shows on hover only while Ctrl is held, as in Windows Explorer, and an experimental, off-by-default option indexes frequently opened folders for instant search. Compressed archives, launcher previews during a drag and search results now have memory limits, and the share mount helper only rolls back what its own setup changed. Large cached folders, fast file operations and custom folder icons take less time.

Copies, drags and new folders work as in Windows Explorer: a copy is named “name - Copy”, a plain drag moves within a drive and copies to another, and New folder makes the folder at once to rename in place. Properties shows Size on disk, a rename that changes the extension asks first, and Super+E can open OpenXplorer on KDE Plasma. An empty folder looks as it does in Windows and takes right-click, paste and drops, New and Paste are off in a folder you cannot write to, Apply to all folders uses the choices in the dialog, and Show after moving items to the Recycle Bin opens it.

Adds item check boxes as in Windows 11 and a redesigned Settings page with eight pages, a search across all of them and details in ⓘ bubbles. Open and Save dialogs no longer wait on network shares and say why Save cannot save, and a folder's expand arrow stays inside its row's highlight. Dropping files onto a file on a Windows drive or share no longer runs it unless it really is a program, and asks first.

Adds Windows Explorer's Group by, separate from the sort, and Folder Options' Apply to all folders and Reset folders. Copies ask about one unreadable file instead of failing the folder and about names Windows cannot use, TAR archives get the ZIP safety limits, read-only and disconnected drives say so, and the Open and Save dialogs no longer freeze or get stuck.
